fatal_errors: The proposed as-cast polycrystalline material and room-temperature-only testing do not reproduce the homogenized FCC single-crystal, orientation-controlled, 9–1373 K comparison needed to separate intrinsic glide resistance, cryogenic inertia, and high-temperature solute pinning.

Changing composition to alter atomic-size mismatch does not independently control lattice distortion; it simultaneously changes chemistry, magnetism, elastic constants, stacking-fault energy, and solute–dislocation interactions.

XRD peak broadening is not a specific measure of static local lattice distortion because crystallite size, dislocation density, residual stress, and compositional heterogeneity can produce the same signal.
explanation: The hypothesis captures one important component of the target: composition-dependent local lattice distortion can increase solid-solution resistance to dislocation glide, and a same-phase, lower-distortion baseline with a correlation-based falsification test is directionally appropriate. However, it omits most of the governing behavior established by the target: temperature-dependent CRSS, thermally activated glide, phonon-drag-controlled inertial dulling below roughly 60–77 K, and Mn/Fe-dependent Cottrell-type Portevin–Le Chatelier pinning at elevated temperature. It also substitutes polycrystalline yield and hardening measurements for orientation-controlled single-crystal CRSS, strain-rate jumps, serration analysis, TEM dissociation-width measurements, and MSAD calculations. The proposed brittle-failure trade-off is speculative and unsupported by the cited record. No prior evidence is supplied, so the evidence requirement is unmet despite a clearly stated falsification rule.
